scientific_hypothesis: Relaxing thickness bounds by ±10% and applying deterministic coordinate-wise perturbation of ±4.0 nm to worst-performing 25% of candidates will increase valid candidate density above 10 and escape local symmetry clusters, leading to improved best_target_score.
expected_advantages: Higher valid candidate density enables better statistical sampling
Perturbation breaks local symmetry to escape suboptimal minima
Maintains proven 24-layer topology from prior successful iterations
known_risks: Relaxed bounds may increase total coating thickness beyond practical limits
Perturbation may temporarily degrade best_target_score during exploration phase
expected_observations: If the periodic hypothesis holds, best_target_score should increase with optimization rounds and stabilize as thicknesses converge to quarter-wave values near 375 nm center wavelength
If the periodic hypothesis fails, best_target_score will plateau below acceptable levels and tightest_margin will not improve across rounds, indicating bandwidth limitation
valid_candidates should remain high (above 10 per round) if the design space is well-conditioned
thicknesses_nm should converge to values near 90-100 nm for HfO2 and 130-140 nm for SiO2 if quarter-wave condition at 375 nm is optimal
stop_conditions: If best_target_score improves by less than 1e-3 against the historical best for two consecutive rounds, treat the axis as exhausted, stop and keep the current best
If valid_candidates falls below 5 for three consecutive rounds, relax thickness bounds and continue for one more round before stopping
